messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT 1987654321: solstice-ai tenant check 'embed-serving-health' firing -> 1200 errors/min, paging @maya :rotating_light:
maya: acked. seeing noise on that customer check for last ~10m, looks like bursts not sustained. digging.
carl: reported by synthetic? which check exactly?
oncall-bot: Check details: metric=embed_service.errors rate=per_min window=1m scope=tenant:solstice-ai, configured threshold=100 errors/min
maya: yep synthetic + prod traffic. quick look at traces shows timeouts from grpc pool to gpu-node-47.
jamie: is it a platform-wide issue or isolated?
maya: isolated to solstice region-us-west-2 and mostly long tail RPCs. other tenants fine.
sre-rotation: tagging this as tenant-impacting. paging policy says escalate if >5 pages in 15m. this is page 1 but noisy.
carl: can we suppress pager for this check while we triage? want to avoid page storm for oncall.
maya: preparing a temporary mute for that check for 30m while I restart the connection pool. will update when done.
ops-jen: +1 on suppression. please add annotation so we know it was intentional.
maya: muting via /incidents mute check embed-serving-health tenant:solstice-ai 30m --reason "connection-pool flapping, in-flight mitigation"
oncall-bot: Mute applied to check embed-serving-health (tenant:solstice-ai) for 30 minutes by maya.
jamie: while muted, can we reduce sensitivity instead of full mute? if bursts come back we won't know. maybe bump threshold to 200 errors/min and add a 3m rolling window.
maya: good call. I'll patch the alert rule: threshold=200 window=3m and keep mute as backup.
carl: please post the exact PromQL so we can audit.
maya: PromQL: sum(rate(embed_service_errors_total{tenant="solstice-ai"}[1m])) by (tenant) * 60
  Proposed rule change: alert if >200 for 3m.
jamie: also create a dashboard panel showing per-node latencies + RPC error types for solstice. put it on the oncall board.
maya: creating dashboard now: dashboard id 8721, panel links: https://graf.redwood/d/8721/solstice-embed-health
ops-jen: while maya restarts pool, is there customer-facing impact? sales is asking.
maya: temporary 5-10% of requests for solstice seeing 500s during bursts. not a full outage, but SLA risk if sustained. informing CS now.
sre-rotation: flagged as 'customer-impact-maybe' in incident tracker: https://inc.redwood/1987654321
carl: after restart of gpu-node-47, what next?
maya: restarted pool on host, tail of logs shows successful reconns. error rate dropped to ~25/min. removing alert mute but keeping rule change for 2h as we monitor.
oncall-bot: Mute removed by maya.
jamie: add a short-lived suppression rule to avoid re-paging during the next deploy window (we have a deploy in 40m).
maya: noted. scheduled a silence 40m-80m for the check.
ops-jen: filing follow-up ticket to investigate root cause: ticket RW-6543 - solstice embed grpc timeout tail. includes heap of traces and node metrics.
carl: sample log snippet recorded in ticket RW-6543: ```
2026-03-14T21:12:03Z host=gpu-node-47 rpc=EmbedService.Infer duration_ms=2400 err=deadline_exceeded
2026-03-14T21:12:04Z host=gpu-node-47 pool=grpc-conn-12 state=stalled
```
jamie: put a post-mortem on calendar for tomorrow 11am, attendees: eng-runtime, eng-sre, solstice account lead.
maya: will add action items: (1) increase pool timeouts for tenant if transient, (2) add backpressure metric on per-tenant queue, (3) tune alert to be percentile-based instead of raw count.
sre-rotation: closing live paging. assign follow-ups to eng-runtime and platform.
ops-jen: thanks, everyone. please update the ticket when you have the config diff. :thumbsup:
maya: pushed alert rule diff to PR #492 in infra-alerts. link: https://git.redwood/p/infra-alerts/pulls/492
carl: nice. once PR merges, enumerate who reviewed and why threshold chosen. want to avoid knee-jerk reduction.
maya: added reviewers jamie, carl. note in PR: threshold=200 chosen after 10m median sampling and to cover short bursts. will revisit after 24h.
jamie: thanks. will follow up in post-mortem.
ops-jen: marking thread resolved in channel, leaving logs for the shift.
oncall-bot: Thread incident 1987654321 marked resolved by ops-jen at 1987654390
